title: Exporting at 2x draws the text sharp instead of blowing the picture up
goal: Exporting a redline at 2x makes a bigger file but not a sharper one: the app finishes the picture at the document size and then enlarges it, so the words come out just as soft as they were. A 2x export should have letters with hard edges.
notes:
DocumentRenderer.render(_:store:scale:) still composites at 1x and applies CILanczosScaleTransform. The machinery to do it properly landed on 2026-09-04: composite document.magnified(by: scale) with contentScale: scale, the way renderTile does. Left out of that task because it changes the pixels every existing export test pins.

Done 2026-09-04. render(_:store:scale:) in DocumentRenderer.swift now mirrors renderTile. The second half of the fix matters as much as the first: stored bitmaps are Lanczos-enlarged in ciImage(for:) (gated on enlargesPhoto, i.e. .image content, contentScale > 1, not magnifyNearest) so the capture keeps the quality the old whole-composite Lanczos gave it. clampedToExtent before the filter is load-bearing: without it the export gets a faded rim. Playtest walks can now render at a scale: { "do": "render", "name": "x", "scale": 2 }.
acceptance: A label exported at 2x has visibly sharper edges than the same label exported at 1x and scaled up
Exporting at 1x produces exactly the pixels it does today
Export timing for a 12 megapixel document does not get worse

log.note: Adversarial review before building: the task said composite the magnified document, full stop. Taken literally that trades one softness for another, because the capture under the redline stops getting the good enlargement it used to get from the Lanczos pass over the whole composite, and the capture is most of what a redline export IS. Measured it on a striped fixture: hard-edge share 0.20 against 0.40. So the short version is crisp composite PLUS keeping the good resampler for stored bitmaps.

Built: render(_:store:scale:) composites document.magnified(by: scale) with contentScale: scale, canvasSize rounded to whole output pixels. ciImage(for:) enlarges stored bitmaps with CILanczosScaleTransform when a magnified render blows them up, clampedToExtent first and cropped back (without the clamp the kernel fades a rim around the picture; a fractional-scale test caught it). 1x and every downscale untouched.

Tests: ScaledRenderTests gained sharper-than-the-old-path, export-equals-the-canvas-tile, 1x-is-byte-for-byte, no-faded-corners, fractional-scale, and capture-no-softer-than-it-was. RenderPerfTests gained exports12MPDocumentAtTwoWithinBudget. Playtest render step takes an optional scale (PhotonzCore + harness + a parse test). Full suite 2908 green.

Perf: 12MP/10-layer 2x export ~88ms median against ~93ms for the old path, with pixels forced (createCGImage is lazy, so measuring without forcing them reported a bogus 0.3ms). Crisp tile 9.0/9.3/9.7ms at 200/400/800%, was 9.2/9.5/9.8ms.

Adversarial review after building, on the probe: ran a walk that opens a capture, places a measurement and renders at 1x and 2x. The chip goes from fuzzy to sharp, stacked in queue/audits/2026-09-04-sharp-2x-export-1.png. Still rough: the Export dialog promises nothing about sharpness, and the capture underneath is inherently an enlargement, so the two halves of a 2x export read differently up close.

Export at 2x composites the whole document at 2x (the canvas's crisp path) instead of enlarging a 1x picture, and stored bitmaps keep the Lanczos enlargement so the capture underneath is no softer than before. Verified on the probe with a playtest that renders at 1x and 2x: chip goes from fuzzy to sharp (queue/audits/2026-09-04-sharp-2x-export.json). 1x export is byte for byte unchanged; 12MP 2x export ~88ms against ~93ms before. Full suite 2908 green, pushed as 8e022d7.
